claim: United Airlines controls 67% of Washington Dulles total passenger traffic, carrying approximately 19.7 million of the airport's 29 million passengers in 2025, and operates 50 jetbridge-equipped gates in Concourses C and D.
source_title: How United Is Quietly Rebuilding Washington Dulles Into Its Ultimate Hub
supporting_excerpt: United controls 67% of Dulles' total traffic, carrying approximately 19.7 million of the airport's 29 million passengers in 2025. The carrier operates 50 jetbridge-equipped gates in Concourses C and D.
units: percent of enplaned passengers; passenger count; jetbridge gate count
caveat: Secondary trade press synthesis of MWAA and United public data; anchor share is directional but not the primary airline-share disclosure MWAA would use in a rate-setting context.

claim: Washington Dulles recorded 29.01 million passengers in 2025 with 10.53 million international travelers, roughly 36% of total traffic — the highest 2025 growth rate among the fifty largest U.S. airports at 6.4% year-over-year.
source_title: How United Is Quietly Rebuilding Washington Dulles Into Its Ultimate Hub
supporting_excerpt: Dulles recorded 10.53 million international travelers in 2025 — a notably high proportion representing 36% of total airport traffic ... record 29.01 million passengers in 2025 (6.4% year-over-year increase) and 'the highest growth rate of the nation's 50 largest airports.'
caveat: Secondary reporting of MWAA traffic; consistent with airport-context packet.

claim: American Airlines is the dominant carrier at Reagan National with a 53% market share by the end of 2024, more than five times the number of routes of its nearest competitors, and moved roughly 14 million passengers through DCA in 2024.
source_title: American Airlines' Most Popular Routes From Its Washington DC Hub
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines is the dominant carrier at DCA, with a 53% market share by the end of 2024, and more than five times the number of routes of its nearest competitors ... the carrier moving 14 million passengers in and out of DCA last year.
caveat: Trade press; 'market share' basis (slots vs seats vs enplanements) not disaggregated.

claim: MWAA signed a new 15-year Airline Use and Lease Agreement effective January 1, 2025, covering a $9 billion capital construction program ($6.99B at IAD, $2.39B at DCA), with a 140% airline-funded debt service coverage target and hybrid full-cost-recovery structure; the agreement required signature by airlines representing a majority of the airports' flights to take effect.
source_title: Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority Completes Negotiations for New Use and Lease Agreement with Airlines
supporting_excerpt: The 15-year pact, which includes a new $9 billion capital construction program, must be signed by airlines representing a majority of the airports' flights, before taking effect on January 1, 2025 ... continued ability to recover all major costs associated with operating the airports ... airline-funded debt service coverage to ensure at least a 140-percent target ratio.
caveat: MWAA-issued release; the operative agreement itself was not read for this brief. Specific MII cost thresholds and exempt project categories are not disclosed in the release.

claim: A majority-in-interest (MII) clause gives the airlines that account for the majority of the traffic at an airport the right to review and accept or veto any capital projects that could lead to significant increases in the rates they pay.
source_title: Majority In Interest of Airlines (MII) Sample Clauses
supporting_excerpt: An MII clause gives the airlines that account for the majority of the traffic at an airport the right to review and accept or veto any capital projects that could lead to significant increases in the rates that they pay for the use of airport facilities.
caveat: Generic legal definition; MWAA-specific MII threshold, exempt categories, and voting mechanics not confirmed here.

claim: MWAA's DCA-IAD system is classified as hybrid residual, with net remaining revenues split per a defined revenue-sharing formula in the Airline Agreement.
supporting_excerpt: At DCA and IAD, operated by the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, net remaining revenues are split per a defined revenue-sharing formula in the Airline Agreement.
caveat: DWU characterizes the MWAA structure as 'hybrid residual'; MWAA's own release describes 'continued ability to recover all major costs' consistent with a hybrid full-cost-recovery model. Terminology varies across analysts; both point to shared risk/reward with airlines.

claim: IAD signatory cost per enplanement was $12.88 in FY2024 and $9.56 in FY2025; DCA CPE was $9.05 in FY2024 and $7.49 in FY2025.
source_title: Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) | Airport Finance | DWU Consulting
caveat: Consulting-aggregated MWAA financial data; DCA figures cross-referenced from the same source's DCA page.

claim: MWAA 2026 first-half signatory landing fee is $2.32 per 1,000 pounds at IAD and $2.57 per 1,000 pounds at DCA.
source_title: Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) | Airport Finance | DWU Consulting
supporting_excerpt: Signatory landing fee: $2.32 per 1,000 lbs, effective 2026-01-01.
caveat: DCA figure taken from parallel DWU DCA page.

claim: An airline briefing referenced by Cranky Flier estimated cost per enplanement under the full IAD transformation plan at $90.64, versus IAD's then-current $12.88.
source_title: The Plan for Dulles is Ambitious and Ridiculous… and It Won't Happen
supporting_excerpt: An airline briefing estimated CPE at '$90.64' under the full plan, compared to IAD's current $12.88 — a seven-fold increase that would make the airport economically unviable for carriers.
caveat: Cranky Flier (Brett Snyder) attributes the $90.64 figure to an 'airline briefing' rather than to a MWAA disclosure; treat as directional airline-side view, not MWAA published number.

claim: Brett Snyder characterized Scott Kirby's posture at the July 2026 IAD transformation announcement as reluctant, quoting: 'There is no world where he wants to pay to operate at this kind of palace' and describing Kirby's implied strategy as taking the pieces he wants and shelving the rest under a future administration.
source_title: The Plan for Dulles is Ambitious and Ridiculous… and It Won't Happen
supporting_excerpt: Despite United CEO Scott Kirby trying not to look too disturbed in the background, there is no world where he wants to pay to operate at this kind of palace ... I'm sure he's using this as a way to get some of the work done that he thinks is most important, and then he figures when a new president is in place, the rest can be shelved.
caveat: Analyst interpretation of the anchor carrier's posture; not a United statement.

claim: Concourse E at IAD is a 435,000 sq ft, 14-gate facility opening late 2026 with a 40,000 sq ft United Club and 46,000 sq ft of concessions, funded by a mix of United, MWAA, and federal infrastructure grants at a project cost exceeding $500 million.
source_title: United and MWAA celebrate $500 million Concourse E expansion to enhance passenger experience at Dulles
supporting_excerpt: The 435,000-square-foot, 14-gate concourse will feature an expansive new United Club location and state-of-the-art customer amenities, expected to debut in late 2026. The project, valued at more than $500 million, was funded through a mix of United and airport investment along with federal infrastructure grants.
caveat: Trade press; capital split percentages between MWAA, United, and federal grants not disclosed.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport program removed over 90 minutes of unnecessary daily announcement time and achieved a reduction of more than 40 percent in overall onsite noise; boarding and departure announcements were retained in the immediate boarding area only, while 'final call' announcements were discontinued airport-wide.
source_title: San Francisco Airport Removed 90 Minutes of Daily Noise — Travelers Say It Changed Everything
supporting_excerpt: successfully removed over 90 minutes of unnecessary daily noise and achieved a reduction of more than 40 percent in overall onsite noise ... airlines making boarding and departure announcements in the immediate boarding area only, while 'final call' announcements are discontinued through the airport.
units: minutes of daily announcement time; percent noise reduction
caveat: Reported figures from SFO/press; measurement methodology (dB weighting, sampling geometry) not verified from a primary SFO Airport Commission document.

claim: London City Airport has operated a silent terminal policy since 2008 in which no tannoy announcements are made throughout the departure lounge; announcements are used only for bad weather or emergency.
source_title: Silent Airport Policy | London City Airport
supporting_excerpt: London City airport has introduced a silent terminal policy in which no tannoy announcements are to be made throughout the departure lounge ... From 2008 ... announcements over the speakers are only used in the case of bad weather or an emergency.
caveat: LCY is a single-runway, short-haul-heavy, no-hubbing airport with a different operating model than IAD or DCA.

claim: ACRP Research Report 175 recommends maintaining a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 dB(A) and a minimum Speech Transmission Index (STI) of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges.
source_title: Chapter 10 — Public Address System Announcements | Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems (ACRP Research Report 175)
supporting_excerpt: The study recommends maintaining an SNR of 10 dB(A) and a minimum STI of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges to ensure that announcements are clearly audible to passengers.
caveat: ACRP guidance, not FAA mandate; adoption at MWAA would need to be through the Design Manual.

claim: At preferential-use airport gates the holdroom (including the agent podium and its PA infrastructure) is the airline's leased premises, and airlines can create and manage their own automated pre-boarding and boarding sequences through gate PA systems.
source_title: Airport Gates: Definitions, Allocation, and Financial Structure
supporting_excerpt: Common-Use Gates: At common-use gates, the holdroom is airport-owned and charged per turn, per seat, or per enplaned passenger. Preferential-Use Gates: For preferential-use lessees, the holdroom is typically the leased premises, priced at the terminal rental rate in dollars per square foot per year.
caveat: Generic industry description; MWAA-specific gate arrangement (preferential vs common-use at IAD Concourses C/D and at DCA) not confirmed here from an MWAA document.

claim: SITA's airport PA solution supports airline-controlled paging from more than 100 full-function stations at ticket counters, baggage claim, and gate podiums, with FIDS integrated to PA.
supporting_excerpt: More than 100 full-function paging stations are in use at ticket counters, baggage claim areas and gate podiums ... FIDS seamlessly integrates with other applications or third-party airport IT solutions, including public address (PA) systems.
caveat: Vendor marketing material; illustrative of industry norm rather than an MWAA-specific installation.

claim: In December 2024 DOT awarded 10 additional daily beyond-perimeter slot exemptions at DCA (5 nonstop round-trips) to Alaska (SEA), American (SAN), Delta (SFO), Southwest (SAT), and United (LAS) under the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, with service starts staggered from February through March 2025.
source_title: Reagan National Airport Slot and Perimeter Rules and Exemptions Authorized in 2024
supporting_excerpt: authorized 10 additional daily beyond-perimeter slot exemptions at DCA (5 nonstop round-trips) ... DOT awarded these in December 2024 to Alaska (SEA), American (SAN), Delta (SFO), Southwest (SAT), and United (LAS).

claim: Following the January 29, 2025 midair collision at DCA (67 fatalities), the FAA on March 14, 2025 removed the section of Helicopter Route 4 between Hains Point and the Woodrow Wilson Bridge from charts and restricted runways 15/33 and 4/22 during specific helicopter operations near DCA.
source_title: Reagan National Airport Slot and Perimeter Rules and Exemptions Authorized in 2024
supporting_excerpt: on March 14, 2025 the FAA removed the section of Helicopter Route 4 between Hains Point and the Woodrow Wilson Bridge from charts and restricted runways 15/33 and 4/22 during specific helicopter operations near DCA.
caveat: CRS summary; underlying FAA notices are the primary source but were not fetched for this brief.
